Group 1 (Case 1):
Here is the student’s answer for this case:
1. Case 1: Lightning-induced eye injury
Vision loss began four days after a forehead lightning strike. Initial exam was normal, but follow-up OCT showed delayed macular thickening and outer retinal disruption at two weeks, partially restored at four months, plus cataract. These temporally linked findings cannot be explained by functional vision loss or pre-existing disease; the delayed pattern fits lightning injury. Missing slit-lamp/ERG and unverified cataract limit certainty, but lightning-induced eye injury is most probable.

Here is the reference diagnosis for this case:
1. Case 1: Lightning-induced retinopathy with delayed-onset cystoid macular abnormalities
